questions.q: What are the four schemas this lesson names for the layering convention used through the rest of the course?
options: raw, staging, warehouse, and reporting
bronze, silver, gold, and platinum
dev, test, staging, and production
extract, transform, load, and archive
questions.explain: The convention splits into four schemas: raw (unmodified landing), staging (cleaned), warehouse (the star schema), and reporting (views for BI tools).

questions.q: Why is 'warehouse' split into a separate schema from 'reporting' rather than combined into one?
options: So a BI tool never connects directly to the fact and dimension tables — it connects to a reporting view sitting in front of them
Snowflake requires star schema tables and views to live in different databases
Reporting schemas cannot contain any SQL objects other than tables
There is no real reason; the split is purely arbitrary
questions.explain: Separating reporting from warehouse means BI connections always go through a view layer, not directly against the underlying fact/dimension tables.

questions.q: In the example reporting view, what does the is_current = TRUE filter accomplish?
options: It ensures the view joins each fact to the SCD2 dimension version that was current, without the report author needing to know SCD2 exists
It filters out all historical fact rows from the fact table
It prevents the view from ever returning more than one row
It disables incremental loading for the underlying tables
questions.explain: Because SCD2 keeps multiple historical rows per natural key, filtering for is_current = TRUE in the view ensures the join picks the currently active dimension version automatically.

questions.q: What is the end-to-end order data moves through across the four schemas?
options: Land it in raw, clean it into staging, model it into warehouse, expose it through reporting
Expose it, model it, clean it, then land it
Model it before landing any data at all
All four steps happen simultaneously in one statement
questions.explain: The pipeline flows raw (COPY INTO) -> staging (CTAS) -> warehouse (MERGE-based modeling) -> reporting (views) in that order.

questions.q: According to the lesson, what does this four-schema layering convention set up for later chapters?
options: RBAC in Chapter 9 (scoped roles per schema) and the Chapter 15 capstone, which asks students to build this exact shape end-to-end
It has no relevance to any later chapter in the course
It replaces the need for virtual warehouses entirely
It is only used for the free preview lesson and nowhere else in the course
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly foreshadows Chapter 9's per-schema RBAC roles and Chapter 15's capstone project, which builds this same four-schema pipeline against real data.
